featureTagline: A paced swim set from your minutes, pool and gear. One unlock, no ads, no account.
_comment: The composed visual identity for this slot, read by scripts/store-studio.py and by scripts/core/palette.mjs. Everything the studio draws - the launcher icon, the adaptive-icon vectors in app/src/main/res/drawable, the feature graphic and the screenshot compositions - is derived from `mark` and `palette` here, so this file is the one place the store presence is decided. It is not optional: the studio refuses to render without it, because falling back to the generic renderer changes the whole pack while store/graphics.md keeps describing the composed one.
_mark: `mark-clock` is a pool-deck pace clock: one bold ring for the bezel, a bold minute hand running to 60 degrees and a bold hour hand back to 200, the pair meeting at the pivot. It is a drawn glyph, not a borrowed one, and it is registered in scripts/lib/icon_design.py's MARK_REGISTRY as three primitives - a `ring` in `paper` and two `stroke` polylines in `amber` and `paper` - so the studio, the launcher vectors and the in-app BrandMark are the same geometry from one source. There are no letters, no numerals and no words, so it reads at 48dp and survives translation. It is a different glyph from every other registered mark (`pipe`, `mark-book`, `mark-stripes`): the ring's outer edge lands exactly on the circle keyline, and the two arms of unequal length at 60 and 200 degrees are what say `a time to swim` rather than `a gauge`.
_palette: One deliberate identity, shared with the app's own theme (app/src/main/java/com/gexetr/laneset/ui/theme/Color.kt) and with the slot's own extended roles in ui/components/Brand.kt: a chlorinated pool blue for the field and the ink, dawn amber for the mark's second hand, and a pace-clock gold that is reserved for the one number the app exists to print - a target time. Roles the studio draws with: `ink`/`ink_soft`/`ink_lift` are the three ends of the background gradient and `accent_deep` the cool glow that gives the field depth; `lane` and `primary` are the lane-rope and the sky-on-water blue the dark scheme paints with, `onPrimary` their ink; `paper` is the whiteboard and the display text; `muted` and `outline` are secondary text and the hairline; `background`/`surface`/`surfaceVariant` and `onSurface`/`onSurfaceVariant` are the pre-dawn deck the phone is photographed on; `secondary` and `rest` are the recovery mint; `amber`/`amber_deep`/`amber_pale` are the mark's second hand and its two steps; `pace` is the target time and nothing else; `warning` is a set the swimmer cannot hold; `bezel`/`bezel_rim` are the device mock-up frame. The `pace` role was moved off the amber hue deliberately: at `#FFC48F` it sat 7.6 degrees and C13.9 from `amber_pale` at 1.20:1, which palette.mjs rule 21 reports as two roles a user cannot tell apart, so the target time is now a gold at H82 that no other role can be mistaken for.
_claim_bounds: Every headline must be true of the shipped build. It computes a session from the user's own constraints, prints a target time derived from two time trials, shares the set as text, prints a card, parses a coach's set, and restores a session that was interrupted. It does not sync between devices, does not connect to a watch, does not read a pace from a device, and does not know the user's historical results. So `Syncs to your watch` is false and `Remembers every session you swam` is a guarantee the app cannot make. Each headline below names something the app verifiably does, and the shot behind it is asserted by store/journey.json.
_headlines: One headline per journey shot, in journey order, kept to 3-5 words so it stays readable at thumbnail size, and each kicker is the one-to-two-word section name that sits above it. The studio falls back to the shot title when this list is short, so a short list would silently change the pack.
_palette_roles_minimum: The declared set is the identity palette the pack renderer draws with, not every Material 3 role: `background`, `surface`, `surfaceVariant`, `primary`, `onPrimary`, `secondary`, `onSurface`, `onSurfaceVariant` and `outline` are all present, plus the domain roles `pace`, `rest`, `lane` and `warning`. Color.kt declares the remaining Material 3 slots (the `on-` pairs, the containers, `inverseSurface`) as constants derived from these 24, which is what palette.agreement reads.
